pll1d19c12-d1e3477.summary: States that although God is called triune, he should not be called triple, since there is no triplicity where there is supreme unity and undifferentiated equality.
claims: God is triune but not triple.

pll1d19c12-d1e3482.summary: Cites De Trinitate VI: God is not triple because he is a Trinity; otherwise the Father alone or Son alone would be less than both together. Since each is as great as all three together, God is in no way triple. With the Son and Spirit the Father is not a greater God, since that perfection cannot grow; each is perfect God, so God is rather called Trinity than triple.
claims: If God were triple, each person would be less than all three.
Each person is as great as all three.

pll1d19c12-d1e3511.summary: Contrasts bodies, where one is less than three and two more than one, with the Trinity, where one person is as great as three, two as one, and they are infinite, without limit of greatness (Ps 144:3). This explains how each is in each, all in each, each in all, all in all, and one is all.
claims: In bodies three are more than one.
In the Trinity one person is as great as three.
The persons are infinite in themselves.
Each is in each, all in each, each in all, and all in all.

pll1d19c12-d1e3532.summary: Concludes that it has been sufficiently shown how no person exceeds another in magnitude.
claims: No person exceeds another in magnitude.

pl-l1d19c12.summary: Concludes that God, though called triune (trinus), should not be called triple (triplex), since there is no triplicity where there is supreme unity and undifferentiated equality. With Augustine: if God were triple, the Father alone would be less than Father and Son together; but each is as great as all three, and that perfection cannot grow. In bodily things one is less than three, but in the Trinity one person is as great as three, and the persons are infinite. This also explains how each is in each, all in each, each in all, and all in all.
claims: God is called triune but not triple.
There is no triplicity in God, since there is supreme unity and equality.
Each person is as great as all three together.
In the Trinity one person is as great as three, and they are infinite in themselves.
Each person is in each, all in each, each in all, and all in all.
